content.title: Master - Definition, Meaning & Synonyms
content.text: SKIP TO CONTENT Other forms: masters; mastered; mastering The original of something (like a recording) is the master. Masters are also experts in fields, from karate to painting. Master actors are brilliant actors: they've mastered the skill of acting: maybe they have a Master of Fine Arts degree. It takes a long time to master anything. The master is the head of a school. People with servants, pets, and (during a horrible period in our history) slaves were called masters. A master key opens many doors, and when you master something, you are extremely good at it. An A+ on a test shows you mastered the material. Definitions of master noun a person who has general authority over others noun directs the work of others see moresee less types: spymastersomeone who directs clandestine intelligence activities type of: employera person or firm that employs workers noun presiding officer of a school noun an officer who is licensed to command a merchant ship see moresee less examples: Captain KiddScottish sea captain who was hired to protect British shipping in the Indian Ocean and then was accused of piracy and hanged (1645-1701) adjective most important element “the master bedroom” “a master switch” verb have dominance or the power to defeat over “Her pain completely mastered her” “The methods can master the problems” see moresee less types: officerdirect or command as an officer dragoonsubjugate by imposing troops enslavemake a slave of; bring into servitude noun an artist of consummate skill “a master of the violin” “one of the old masters” see moresee less types: old mastera great European painter prior to 19th century noun an authority qualified to teach apprentices see moresee less type of: authorityan expert whose views are taken as definitive noun a combatant who is able to defeat rivals verb have a firm understanding or knowledge of; be on top of see moresee less types: cinchget a grip on; get mastery of type of: knowknow how to do or perform something verb be or become completely proficient or skilled in “She mastered Japanese in less than two years” see moresee less type of: knowknow how to do or perform something verb get on top of; deal with successfully see moresee less types: bulldogthrow a steer by seizing the horns and twisting the neck, as in a rodeo noun someone who holds a master's degree from academic institution noun key that secures entrance everywhere see moresee less types: skeleton keya passkey with much of the bit filed away so that it can open different locks type of: keymetal device shaped in such a way that when it is inserted into the appropriate lock the lock's mechanism can be rotated noun an original creation (i.e., an audio recording) from which copies can be made see moresee less type of: creationan artifact that has been brought into existence by someone "Master."
